items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Dave Pell, who has the octet, he distributes them for me.

ctx.x: tell you what I need now.” I’m the band leader, there was something I wanted to hear. You know, right or wrong, I wanted to hear something that I wanted. It started with, “You hear how the lead trumpet player, how you can hear him so well?” “Yeah.” I said, “Now let me hear the fourth trumpet player. All four trumpets. On the same level.” I wanted to hear the sound of a band, not protruding notes. Now great, now you hear? In the old days, by the way, it was hard to record the bass. All you heard was boom-boom-…

want that cut out. He said, “Let me show you. Let me do something for you. Don’t listen to those things at all anymore,” which I hardly ever did because they were on reel to reel. And he cut it to where we made it into a five minute thing where it was almost like it started out, the ensemble, it was an ensemble. Because that was what made the band. Even though we had the greatest soloists, there was the fire of the ensemble, because they played so well together. I mean you find a lot of bands playing but not…
